events.title: Verhalenhuis
events.description:
Het Verhalenhuis offers storytelling workshops to people who have often had no prior contact with the performing arts and whose stories are underrepresented in society's mainstream narrative. Each Verhalenhuis edition consists of a series of 6-8 weekly workshops in which participants work on structuring stories and using body language and voice when sharing them.

During the Hague Justice week we are having a kick off for a new group in the Hague Humanity Hub together with Pitztop. The session is meant for 8-10 newcomers who want to get acquainted with theatermaking and storytelling. 

The skills to tell and present your own story are applicable in almost any field and can contribute to self-confidence and the sense that your story matters. By reclaiming stories under the motto "your story on your terms," participants discover the power of narrative in their own hands. Alongside the workshops, Het Verhalenhuis also offers these stories and storytellers a stage as a follow-up trajectory. Participants in the Verhalenhuis editions are invited to create a theatre production together with theatre-maker Arvand Dashtaray and the Virgule FPAC team. ROSE Stories also curates a digital version of Het Verhalenhuis, where participants can share their stories in digital format.

events.title: Blue on the beauty of De Stijl and the strength of NATO - Exhibit
events.description: Visit an intriguing exhibition at Kunstmuseum Den Haag about aesthetics and politics, focusing  on the visual identity of NATO and modern art by Piet Mondrian, Gerrit Rietveld and artists.

events.title:
Justice and Redress for Survivors of Conflict-Related Sexual Violence at the International Court of Justice.

Panel 1 — Redress for Survivors at the ICJ: Implementation of the DRC v. Uganda Reparations Order
events.description:
During The Hague Justice Week the Dr. Denis Mukwege Foundation will convene three expert panel discussions confronting a question survivors of conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) force us to ask honestly: does international law, and the international justice system built to enforce it, actually change survivors’ lives in practice?  

In panel 1 experts will examine whether Congolese victims and communities have received the compensation the Court intended, and the role of victims, civil society, and the international community in ensuring tangible redress.

events.title:
Justice and Redress for Survivors of Conflict-Related Sexual Violence at the International Court of Justice.  

Panel 2 — Justice for Survivors at the ICJ: The Gambia v. Myanmar Case
events.description:
During The Hague Justice Week  the Dr. Denis Mukwege Foundation will convene three expert panel discussions confronting a question survivors of conflict-related sexual violence  force us to ask honestly: does international law, and the international justice system built to enforce it, actually change survivors’ lives in practice? Not as an abstract legal question, but as a tangible reality for survivors in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Myanmar, and throughout the world — people whose pain has continued for years, and whose right to justice has been delayed even longer.

With judgment expected in late 2026 in The Gambia v. Myanmar Case, this panel explores the legal significance of  conflict-related sexual violence as an underlying act of genocide, survivors’ own expectations of justice, and whether the case can advance peace amid Myanmar’s ongoing civil war.

events.title: International Law as a Compass for Foreign Policy
events.host: Advisory Committee on Public International Law (CAVV)
events.description:
In this session members of the CAVV will present their thoughts on the role of international law in foreign policy and focus on Dutch foreign policy. They will discuss how the Netherlands has always been a proponent of international law and, as a result, The Hague has developed into the capital of Peace and Justice. 

The panel will discuss the following questions: how do current geopolitical developments affect or even threaten the rule-based order and how does The Netherlands position itself in this context? 

The panel is organised in a town hall debate-format where panel members will give short pitches/introductions and actively engage with questions from a lay and expert audience. We hope to achieve an informed and stimulating debate on the current state of international law and how it impacts the position of the Netherlands and The Hague as capital of peace and justice.

events.title: Making Human Rights Law Work: Building new alliances between business, finance & civil society
events.host: European Center for Non-Profit Law (ECNL), ABN AMRO
events.description: Human rights and environmental due diligence laws increasingly require companies and financial institutions to identify, prevent and address adverse human rights impacts. Effective implementation depends on access to reliable, independent information from civil society organisations, journalists, trade unions, researchers and affected communities. However, as civic space faces growing restrictions worldwide, this vital information ecosystem is becoming more vulnerable. This session examines why shrinking civic space is not only a civil society issue, but also a business, banking and justice concern. Bringing together representatives from business, finance, civil society and policy, it will highlight practical examples of cross-sector collaboration, including the Dutch KYC (Know Your Customer) standard to reduce NGO de-risking and research on conducting human rights due diligence in restrictive contexts. Participants will explore how new partnerships can strengthen accountability and help translate human rights laws into effective practice.

events.title:
Justice and Redress for Survivors of Conflict-Related Sexual Violence at the International Court of Justice.

Panel 3 — Beyond the Courtroom: Survivor-Led Advocacy and the Future of Justice for Conflict-Related Sexual Violence (Closing Panel)
events.description:
During The Hague Justice Week the Dr. Denis Mukwege Foundation will convene three expert panel discussions confronting a question survivors of conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) force us to ask honestly: does international law, and the international justice system built to enforce it, actually change survivors’ lives in practice? Not as an abstract legal question, but as a tangible reality for survivors in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Myanmar, and throughout the world — people whose pain has continued for years, and whose right to justice has been delayed even longer.    

Closing The Hague Justice Week, this panel draws together the findings of the DRC v. Uganda and Gambia v. Myanmar panels to ask what comes next. It spotlights the Mukwege Foundation’s and SEMA’s tools for translating legal obligations into survivor-centred practice — including the Guidebook on State Obligations for Conflict-Related Sexual Violence and SEMA’s Call to Action — and considers what “80 years and beyond” of international law must look like if it is to deliver, in practice as much as in principle, on its promise to survivors.

events.title: Justice has no Passport: A Global Conversation on Universal Jurisdiction
events.description:
A virtual conversation on universal jurisdiction. One of the most powerful, yet still underused and often misunderstood, tools for holding perpetrators of the world’s gravest crimes accountable.
Bringing together speakers with diverse regional and professional perspectives, the discussion will explore how universal jurisdiction has evolved, the challenges it faces today, and the role it can play in advancing accountability and international justice in a global order under increasing strain.
The conversation is open to anyone interested in the fight against impunity and the future of international justice—including legal professionals, students, policymakers, and civil society actors.
At a time when the international justice system is facing unprecedented pressure, this session offers an opportunity to hear directly from practitioners working across different contexts to strengthen universal jurisdiction and renew its promise as a tool for justice.

Meet the Speakers:

- Tomas Kevin Manguel, Professor of International Criminal Law at the University of Buenos Aires and Legal Adviser at StraLi

- Marie Wilmet, Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow, Université libre de Bruxelles

- Atilla Kisla, Human rights lawyer, International Justice Cluster Lead at Southern Africa Litigation Centre (SALC)

- Priya Pillai, PhD, International lawyer, and executive director of the Asia Justice Coalition

The session will be moderated by Alessia Schiavon, Executive Director FIBGAR

events.title: Scaling People-Centred Justice with AI
events.venue: Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) office
events.description:
Millions of people across Africa first encounter the justice system not in a courtroom, but at a police station, a checkpoint, or through a phone screen. In Nigeria alone, an estimated 25 million people face legal problems every year, and more than 14 million cannot get the help they need. AI-powered tools are opening new possibilities for delivering legal information, guidance and support at scale and closer to the point of need but scaling them responsibly raises real questions about reliability, privacy, bias, accountability and human oversight.

This interactive session brings together experiences from Nigeria (Justice Padi AI), Tunisia and Niger with justice practitioners, policymakers and technology partners to explore what these emerging models teach us about expanding access to justice across different legal, institutional and infrastructure contexts. Participants will hear a moderated panel discussion and country snapshots, then step into the "From Prototype to Scale-Up" simulation, a board game in which teams take on the role of decision-makers deploying an AI-powered justice solution, navigating real dilemmas around data governance, ethics, institutional resistance, financing and political constraints.

Come for a candid look at what it really takes to move AI-for-justice tools from prototype to sustainable scale, and leave with practical considerations for responsible design, human oversight and institutional collaboration.

events.title: Legal Clinic for Civil Societal Organizations
events.description:
During The Hague Justice Week, Partos and Pro Bono Connect are inviting civil society organisations to seek accessible legal advice from solicitors at various law firms.

Would you like to find out more about what a lawyer does, or would you like to ask for some advice? Do come along!

events.title: One World, One Home, One Law for All: Commemoration Centenary ICJ Judge and Vice-President Christopher Weeramantry (17.11.1926)
events.host: Judicap in co-operation with Sri Lanka Embassy
events.description: Even a century after the establishment of the World Court in 1920, one of the greatest challenges facing international law remains that of bringing the world’s diverse cultures and legal traditions into harmony. Several judges have made exceptional contributions to this endeavour. A prominent figure in recent decades was Christopher Weeramantry of Sri Lanka (ICJ judge, 1991–2000). Throughout his life, he sought common ground among the world’s major religions and emphasized the moral convictions that unite humanity. His principled position in the 1996 advisory proceedings on the legality of the threat or use of nuclear weapons remains as relevant as ever. At the gathering at the Embassy of Sri Lanka, the judge’s former colleagues and students will discuss the significance and feasibility of Weeramantry’s ideas in an era of growing polarisation and the erosion of international law.

events.title: Judging International Justice - featuring Judge Hilary Charlesworth of the International Court of Justice, in conversation with Professor Anna Spain Bradley of UCLA Law
events.host: UCLA Law's The Promise Institute for Human Rights (Europe)
events.description: Join us for this annual event featuring Judge Hilary Charlesworth of the International Court of Justice in discussion with Professor Anna Spain Bradley, MacArthur Foundation Chair in International Justice and Human Rights at UCLA School of Law. The discussion will center on the evolving role of international adjudication and international law in the world today. This lecture series furthers the mission of The Promise Institute and UCLA by supporting public education and engagement with international justice and human rights.

events.title: Jeune Fille, Droit et Souveraineté Économique en Afrique
events.host: Cameroon Ministry of Justice, Reknow Femmes D'Expertise
events.description: Bringing together young people, legal professionals, economic actors, civil society, and more, this session will examine the barriers that limit girls' ability to access and exercise their rights, as well as the role of the law in turning rights into real opportunities. Through expert perspectives, real life experiences, and candid discussions, participants will explore the connection between girls' empowerment, sustainable development, and economic sovereignty. Join us for this interactive session exploring how girls' access to rights can contribute to their individual and collective autonomy as well as Africa's broader economic sovereignty.

events.title: Film Screening: Surviving Genocide – The Rohingya Quest for Justice
events.description:
A screening of a documentary movie, featuring victims and witnesses’ stories and their role in international justice process – and what it means to them and their community. The screening will be followed by a discussion about the first genocide case in decades and potential outcome and the role of victims and witnesses. The documentary focuses on the realities and significance of having victim voices before the International Court of Justice (ICJ). The discussion will also broadly highlight the positive impact of international law at a time that international law and justice institutions are under attack.

This short and poignant documentary offers a unique window into what international legal proceedings mean in practice for the people they are designed to serve. Looking into both technical and humane aspects, the film highlights the importance of the full inclusion of victims in legal processes. It shows what can be achieved when frontline organisations work hand in hand with UN mechanisms and states to support the most vulnerable people. Moving between the front and back stages of the first genocide case in nearly two decades, “Surviving Genocide – The Rohingya Quest for Justice” is a powerful testament to hope and the impact of collective action against hatred and impunity.

events.title: Roundtable on ICJ Jurisprudence
events.host: Columbia Society of International Law & Columbia Journal of Transnational Law
events.description: Hosted by the Columbia Society of International Law and the Columbia Journal of Transnational Law, the session brings together two professors of international law and a group of Columbia Law students and looks at specific ICJ decisions and the questions scholars have not yet fully answered about them.

events.title: The Proposal for an International Anti-Corruption Court: Renewing the Promise of Justice, 80 Years On
events.host: Integrity Initiatives International Europe - III Europe
events.description:
Eighty years ago, the International Court of Justice (CIJ) opened in The Hague to settle disputes between countries. In the decades since, the international community has built new courts to hold individuals accountable for the gravest crimes, from war crimes to genocide. But one crime that does enormous damage still has no international court: grand corruption. Grand corruption, the theft of public money by those at the very top of government, drains hundreds of billions from public budgets every year, funds repression, and erodes people's trust in the institutions meant to protect them. Yet when national courts are unwilling or unable to act, there is often nowhere else to turn.

This session explores a proposal to change that: an International Anti-Corruption Court (IACC), a new court that would hold senior officials criminally accountable and help return stolen assets to the people they were taken from.
You'll hear from a senior official of the International Court of Justice, who will introduce the proposal and reflect on lessons from the Court's 80 years of experience; a former international criminal prosecutor who helped draft the treaty for the IACC; and two human rights defenders who have challenged authoritarian governments in Myanmar and Russia, who will explain how corruption keeps such regimes in power and what real accountability could mean for people on the ground. A moderator from The Hague municipality will guide the conversation, asking why this matters for the city and for governments elsewhere.

he panel will be followed by an open Q&A. Join us for a lively, accessible conversation about how justice can keep pace with the challenges of our time

events.title: Nuremberg Academy Dialogue: The United Nations and the Nuremberg Principles
events.description:
To mark the 80th anniversary of the United Nations (UN) and the International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg, the International Nuremberg Principles Academy will convene a high-level webinar bringing together leading scholars and legal practitioners.

The second Nuremberg Academy Dialogue will examine the foundational role of the United Nations and the International Law Commission in formulating the Nuremberg Principles and consider how these principles still matter today. It will explore how the principles recognised following the Nuremberg trials have shaped international criminal law and continue to inform accountability efforts for core international crimes, alongside current developments in the field. 

Participants will hear from leading experts, including Ambassador David Scheffer, Senior Fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, Professor of Practice at Arizona State University and former US Ambassador-at-Large for War Crimes Issues, and Professor Dr Cécile Aptel, Principal Advisor, UN International, Impartial and Independent Mechanism on Syria, and Professor of Practice of International Law, The Fletcher School, Tufts University. Chaired by Dr Viviane Dittrich, Deputy Director of the International Nuremberg Principles Academy.

events.title: Renewing the Memories #1 - Blue Island Screening & Discussion
events.description:
Renewing the Memories #1 presents a screening of Blue Island (2022), directed by Chan Tze-woon. Blending documentary interviews with re-enactments, the film brings together the personal memories of different generations and connects them with key moments in Hong Kong’s history.
By revisiting experiences of political upheaval, resistance, migration and loss, the film asks how memories can be preserved and passed on when public narratives are being reshaped or erased. It invites us to consider remembrance as an essential part of the continuing pursuit of peace and justice.
After the screening, director Chan Tze-woon will join us online for a live Q&A and discussion.

events.title: Renewing the Memories #2 - The Taoyuan Airport Incident Screening & Discussion
events.description: Renewing the Memories #2 presents The Taoyuan Airport Incident (1986), filmed by Taiwan’s Green Team during the final years of martial law. Through this historical recording, the screening explores how independent images can challenge official narratives, preserve suppressed memories and contribute to the pursuit of democracy and justice.

events.title: Renewing the Memories #3 - Three Castrated Goats - Screening & Discussion
events.description: Set in rural Shaanxi during China’s strict COVID restrictions, "Three Castrated Goats" follows a man who returns home to collect three goats but becomes trapped by quarantine rules. Through dark humour and absurdity, the film reveals how systems of control enter everyday life and affect ordinary people. The film offers another perspective on censorship and the people responsible for enforcing it. Together, the two works invite reflection on freedom of expression, collective memory and life within systems of control. Director Ye Xingyu will join us online for a live Q&A after the screening.
